name: Loperamide
route_note: Oral capsules, tablets or liquid after loose stools, up to a labelled maximum daily dose
owner: generic (many); Imodium brand: Kenvue (Johnson & Johnson heritage)

discovery.by: Paul Janssen and colleagues at Janssen Pharmaceutica
discovery.note: A phenylpiperidine opioid designed to act on the gut with minimal central effects.

tagline: Gut-selective opioid that slows intestinal transit to treat diarrhoea
summary: Loperamide is an opioid agonist that acts on mu receptors in the intestinal wall to slow gut motility. At recommended doses it barely enters the brain, so it is sold over the counter for diarrhoea, but very high doses taken for misuse can cause fatal heart-rhythm disturbances.
mechanism: Loperamide activates mu-opioid receptors on myenteric plexus neurons, reducing acetylcholine and prostaglandin release, decreasing propulsive peristalsis and increasing transit time, which allows more fluid and electrolyte absorption.
It also increases anal sphincter tone. P-glycoprotein efflux at the blood–brain barrier and extensive first-pass metabolism keep central opioid effects minimal at normal doses.
uses: Chronic diarrhoea associated with inflammatory bowel disease

history.title: US approval
history.detail: FDA approves loperamide as a prescription drug.

history.title: OTC
history.detail: Loperamide becomes available over the counter in the US.

history.title: Cardiac warning
history.detail: FDA warns that taking much higher than recommended doses, including for misuse, can cause serious heart problems and death.

history.title: Packaging limits
history.detail: FDA asks makers to sell OTC loperamide in limited quantities in blister packs to deter misuse.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 and CYP2C8 (oxidative N-demethylation); P-gp substrate

serious: QT prolongation, torsades de pointes and cardiac arrest at high doses
Paralytic ileus and toxic megacolon (especially in colitis or children)

facts: Loperamide is structurally related to haloperidol and diphenoxylate.
It should not be used when diarrhoea is accompanied by high fever or bloody stools.
